reused_from: existing NR10 split (docs/learning_runs/real_data_only_learning_check.md); rebuilt byte-reproducibly in this phase using the same script/seed, not a new split

schema_level_leakage_check.method: compared schema_name (NLP4LP relevant_doc_id) sets across train/dev/test
schema_level_leakage_check.finding: every one of the 330 instances has a UNIQUE schema_name; train/dev/test schema-name sets are pairwise disjoint by construction (330 instances = 330 unique schemas)
schema_level_leakage_check.conclusion: no schema-level leakage risk beyond the already-verified instance-level split; an additional schema-disjoint diagnostic split was judged unnecessary since schema-level and instance-level disjointness coincide for this dataset

instance_level_integrity: verified via src.learning.verify_split_integrity (train/dev/test files are distinct, non-identical) and by direct set-intersection check on instance_id (all three pairwise intersections empty)
label_provenance: gold (mention, slot) pairs derived from results/eswa_revision/00_env/nlp4lp_gold_cache.json parameter values, matched to canonically-extracted mention values (tools.nlp4lp_downstream_utility._extract_opt_role_mentions) within relative tolerance 1e-6
claims_this_split_can_support: grounding-quality comparison under an ORACLE (gold) schema assumption -- this split does NOT evaluate schema retrieval, since schema_name is taken directly from NLP4LP relevant_doc_id (gold), not from a retrieval baseline
claims_this_split_cannot_support: a comparison directly against the canonical 331-query TF-IDF-retrieval InstantiationReady figures (0.5287 etc.) -- those numbers are retrieval-conditioned and computed over all 331 queries, not this 50-query oracle-schema subsample; M0 in this phase was therefore re-run on the identical 50-query subset with --baseline oracle for a fair comparison, see docs/LEARNED_GROUNDING_P0.md
